title: Matrix multiplication as composition: interpreting linear transformations via basis vectors (Essence of Linear Algebra, Chapter 4)
summary: 3Blue1Brown’s Essence of Linear Algebra, Chapter 4, presents matrix multiplication as the composition of linear transformations. The video recalls that a linear transformation is determined by the images of the basis vectors i-hat and j-hat, so the matrix columns encode these transformed bases. It then shows how composing two transformations (e.g., rotation followed by a shear) yields a single matrix—the product—that captures the overall effect. The derivation is illustrated both geometrically and numerically: you can obtain the composition matrix by tracking where each basis vector ends up through the sequence, or by applying the left matrix to each column of the right matrix. The right-to-left reading of products follows from function notation. The chapter also covers the order-sensitivity of composition, demonstrates a concrete 2×2 example, generalizes to symbolic matrices, discusses associativity from a transformation viewpoint, and ends by encouraging conceptual understanding over memorization while foreshadowing higher-dimensional extensions in the next video.
topics: columns of a matrix as transformed basis vectors
computing composition matrices from M1 and M2

sections.title: Recap: linear transformations as matrices
sections.description: Recalls that linear transformations are functions on vectors and that a matrix represents such a transformation by recording where i-hat and j-hat land; any vector is a combination of these basis vectors, so the matrix is determined by the images of the basis.

sections.title: Composition of transformations and the composition matrix
sections.description: Describes applying one transformation after another to obtain a new linear transformation, which can be described by a single matrix—the product—that captures the combined effect.

sections.title: Computing the composition matrix from M1 and M2 (column method)
concepts: first column via M2*(first column of M1)
second column via M2*(second column of M1)
sections.description: Shows how the composition matrix is formed by tracking where i-hat and j-hat end up through the two matrices, yielding the columns of the product.

sections.title: General symbolic column method for composition
concepts: left matrix times right matrix columns
sections.description: Extends the column method to matrices with symbolic entries, illustrating that the same reasoning applies to any 2×2 matrices.

sections.title: Interpretation and order in matrix products
sections.description: Emphasizes the geometric meaning of matrix multiplication and why the order matters, tying back to transformation intuition.

sections.title: Associativity explained through transformation thinking
sections.description: Presents why matrix multiplication is associative by viewing it as applying three transformations in a fixed order, rather than algebraic manipulation alone.

sections.title: Encouragement to explore concepts visually and foreshadowing higher dimensions
sections.description: Advocates developing intuition by mentally simulating transformations and their composition, and previews extending ideas beyond two dimensions.
